title: Capacity-aware speculative decode gate with annealing thresholds and staged fallback
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Introduce a runtime admission gate for speculative decoding that is aware of current capacity (GPU queue lengths, kernel contention) and anneals acceptance thresholds over the duration of a request burst. The gate should combine: (1) a confidence delta signal from prefill probes, (2) kernel-affinity scoring to prefer models/kernels that match the request shape, and (3) a soft quota system that prevents explosive speculative fanout under constrained capacity. On rejection, the system performs a staged fallback: fast variant (same model, lower precision), regional fallback, then synchronous decode. Goal: improve overall tail latency and cost while bounding worst-case resource amplification from speculation.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime implements an admission controller that ingests prefill probe score and current capacity signals and returns accept/deny with reason codes.
Annealing schedule configurable per route and per customer; default schedule reduces acceptance threshold linearly over 200ms after burst start.
Kernel-affinity scoring used to prefer fast-path kernels; mismatched kernels increase refusal probability.
Soft quota prevents speculative branching beyond N speculative children per model pool; quota can be burstable with decay.
Fallback chain executes automatically and is observable in the Console with per-request breadcrumbs and fallback_reason tag.

End-to-end tests and canary show <=10% increase in median latency and >=20% reduction in 99.9th percentile resource amplification for heavy speculative workloads compared to current optimistic router baseline.
Telemetry surfaces acceptance_rate, fallback_rate by reason, kernel_mismatch_rate, speculative_branching_factor, and per-route cost delta.
design_decisions: Use confidence delta from prefill probe instead of absolute probability to make acceptance robust across models and prompt styles.
Annealing thresholds chosen to favor low-latency during brief bursts and to avoid starvation by gradually relaxing over time.
Soft quota is per-model-pool + per-customer to avoid noisy neighbor effects; global emergency override exists for SEV situations.
Kernel-affinity is a lightweight fingerprint (attention pattern length + kv-cache footprint) evaluated in the prefill path to avoid extra scheduling hops.
Fallbacks are staged to preserve quality: lower-precision variant (quantized model) => regional replica (same fidelity) => synchronous single-model decode.
Opted for conservative defaults to reduce risk to tail latency; advanced tuning will be exposed via Redwood Optimize later.
implementation_plan: 1) Add admission controller interface in runtime router (RFC in PR #1427).
2) Integrate capacity signals: gpu_queue_ms, active_batches, kernel_contention_score (telemetry hooks already exist in runtime-telemetry service).
3) Implement annealing schedule module and per-route config in control plane; default config shipped in runtime-1.22.
4) Build kernel-affinity fingerprint in prefill path and expose to router for scoring.
5) Implement soft quota book-keeping with lightweight decay (token-bucket style) in model-pool manager.
6) Wire staged fallback executor and enrich Console breadcrumbs + tracing with fallback_reason.
7) Add integration tests: synthetic burst scenarios, kernel mismatch scenarios, cross-region failover tests.
8) Canary rollout to 5% traffic for 48 hours with automatic rollback if fallback_rate or tail latency regress beyond thresholds.
GitHub PRs: runtime#1427 (controller interface), runtime#1439 (kernel fingerprint), controlplane#501 (per-route config schema), console#287 (breadcrumbs UI).
rollout_plan: Alpha deploy on internal cluster serving synthetic chat-load for two days; verify metrics and inspect breadcrumbs.
Canary 5% external traffic for 48h with automated gates (no >5% p99 latency regression, fallback_rate < 5% baseline).
Gradual ramp to 25% for 72h while enabling kernel-affinity logging for offline analysis.
Full rollout after 2-week bake and sign-off from Reliability and Product; include retro and playbook update.
Immediate kill-switch in control plane to disable speculative gating and revert to current optimistic router.
Expose config toggle per-customer to opt-out of speculative gating during onboarding.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: incorrect annealing schedule may allow too much branching leading to resource exhaustion. Mitigation: conservative default + soft quota + emergency override.

Risk: kernel-affinity misclassification could deny fast-path for valid requests. Mitigation: keep fingerprint small, run A/B to collect false denial rate, and include override heuristics based on recent success.
Risk: fallback chain may degrade quality. Mitigation: order fallbacks by fidelity, include per-fallback quality monitoring against evaluation set.
Risk: operational complexity for SRE. Mitigation: dashboards, alerting for new metrics, and playbook with runbook steps.
